content.text: The text combines excerpts from several works. A history of musical instruments traces medieval and post-medieval organs, lutes, viols, bagpipes, bells, carillons, and orchestras. A health primer explains digestion, nutrition, circulation, breathing, skin, senses, exercise, and the harms of alcohol and tobacco. A novel follows Elaine and Davila, abducted from Hampton and held in a remote house by treasure-seeking criminals; Elaine pays their ransom, and the Parmenter jewels are later found in a Hampton cellar. A comedy depicts deafness, deception, and reconciliation in Coddle’s house. Another novel follows Sidney’s nursing career, K. Le Moyne’s concealed identity and love, Max Wilson, Carlotta’s jealousy and attempted poisoning, and the struggles of families on the Street. Christine marries Palmer, whose infidelity causes misery, while Tillie leaves the boarding house for Schwitter’s country home; financial hardship eventually pressures them toward operating it as a disreputable lodging house.
